newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: The rand ended Wednesday just below the 4.70 level after Reserve Bank intervention in the morning pulled the unit back from a morning low bid of 4.7175 on the dollar.
It ended that day at 4.6990/7040 from 4.6950/7000 on Tuesday but weakened to 4.7060/7110 in after-hours trade.

The rand was knocked weaker by dollar demand in New York overnight, in a belated reaction to comments by Trevor Manuel on Tuesday, coupled with local rand sales on Wednesday following remarks by Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals to a local newspaper.
Forex dealers said remarks by Stals on conditions for a "big bang" scrapping of exchnage controls, which could include IMF help, had heightened uncertainty in the market.
"The rand weakened on uncertainty created by Stals' comments on forex policy," a senior trader said.
Another added: "Unless you are saying something clearly it creates an element of uncertainty. What we need is something concrete (on exchange controls) soon."
Traders said the Reserve Bank stepped in at around the 4.7120/7140 level supplying dollars to the market and knocking the rand lower. The Bank kept a presence throughout the day.
"The bank put dollars into the market in what I would describe as quite aggressive action," one noted.
Afternoon trade was subdued in comparison as the rand toyed with the 4.70 level and some London players sold dollars into the market.

Traders expected the rand to test higher levels on Thursday on the back of nervy sentiment and the release of October gold and foreign exchange reserves which are expected to have been drained further due to the ailing rand.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast gross reserves would decline to 9.6 billion rand from 10 billion rand in September, equivalent to just under four weeks import cover.

Against the crosses, the rand had recovered almost four cents from its new low reached against sterling on Tuesday and was last at 7.7148/7291 from 7.7538/7668 overnight and at 0.3226/3230 marks from 0.3218/3222 marks previously.
Bonds ended the day steady after see-sawing around the important 15.90 percent level during the day.
At 1420 GMT the key R150 bond was quoted unchanged from its previous close at 15.89 percent but it weakened back above 15.90 pct to 15.915 pct in after-hours trade.

Dealers said trade had been dictated by option books ahead of the close-out on Thursday. They said the news of the day was a sharp kick up in money market rates as a high money market shortage kept a tight grip on liquidity.
"I expect the market to range between 15.86/87 percent and 15.91/92 percent ahead of the close-out," a senior trader said.
"The overhanging concern is that we could see renewed selling on the back of the tight money market conditions," he added.
Another trader said a vulnerable rand, expectations of a negative reserves figure and a bleak technical picture did not bode well for the short term outlook.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates kicked higher to between 16.75 to 16.90 percent from 16.40 to 16.55 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also higher at between 16.10 to 16.25 percent from 15.75 to 15.90 percent.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.379 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.265 billion rand on Monday.

Money market traders said the rise in short-term rates signalled the market was discounting a hike in the key Bank rate -- currently at 16 percent -- and the present tight situation was likely to remain until early 1997, with Christmas spending looming.
The Bond Exchange said foreigners sold a net 189.94 million rand of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 38.83 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes stood at 4.47 billion rand on Tuesday from 3.37 billion rand on Monday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
